title: Combobox suggestions for large or searchable choices
summary: Use an accessible combobox when users benefit from typing to filter or receive suggestions from a large choice set.
problem: Long static selects are slow to scan, while custom autocomplete widgets often fail keyboard and assistive-technology behavior.
use_when: The option set is large or searching by text materially helps selection
Suggestions can narrow choices without hiding the ability to type
avoid_when: There are only a few stable options
Free text is valid and suggestions would incorrectly imply a closed set
rationale: Comboboxes combine input with a controlled popup and require explicit interaction semantics.
Simpler controls remain preferable when they solve the problem.

use_if: The option set is large or searching by text materially helps selection
Suggestions can narrow choices without hiding the ability to type
prefer_alternatives_if: A native select, radio group, or ordinary text input is simpler and sufficient

requirements: Implement the documented input and popup relationship.
Expose expanded state and active or selected options.
Maintain keyboard access without stealing text-editing keys unexpectedly.
keyboard: Support appropriate arrow-key navigation in the popup and keep Tab behavior predictable.

requirements: Show meaningful matches and a no-results state.
Do not require selection when free text is valid.
Avoid loading huge option sets before needed.
